::: {.solutions}

**Show all your reasoning.** Total: **32 marks** · Suggested time: **45 minutes**.

For every question the method is the same: **rewrite the sentence as "if … then …" first**, then read off
which way the arrow points. Do not try to reason about the meaning in English — that is how arrows get
flipped by accident.

| Section | What it covers | Marks |
|---|---|---|
| **A — Fluency** | translating the four forms; *and / or / not* | 10 |
| **B — Exam standard** | deciding what follows; equivalence | 14 |
| **C — Stretch** | chains of *if and only if*; multi-statement reasoning | 8 |

# Section A — Fluency

## Question 1 **[4]**

$P$ and $Q$ are statements. Write each of the following using $\Rightarrow$ or $\Leftrightarrow$.

&nbsp;&nbsp;(a) $Q$ only if $P$ **[1]**

&nbsp;&nbsp;(b) $Q$ if $P$ **[1]**

&nbsp;&nbsp;(c) $P$ if and only if $Q$ **[1]**

&nbsp;&nbsp;(d) If $Q$ then $P$ **[1]**

*Answer form: an implication such as $P \Rightarrow Q$.*

::: {.workspace style="min-height:5cm"}
Working
:::

## Question 2 **[3]**

Let $n = 30$. State whether each is **true** or **false**.

&nbsp;&nbsp;(a) $n$ is divisible by $4$ **or** $n$ is divisible by $5$. **[1]**

&nbsp;&nbsp;(b) $n$ is divisible by $5$ **and** $n$ is divisible by $6$. **[1]**

&nbsp;&nbsp;(c) $n$ is **not** divisible by $9$. **[1]**

## Question 3 **[3]**

Let $n$ be a positive integer. For each statement, decide whether it is **true** or **false**, and give a
counterexample for any that is false.

&nbsp;&nbsp;(a) $n$ is divisible by $10$ **only if** $n$ is divisible by $5$. **[1]**

&nbsp;&nbsp;(b) $n$ is divisible by $10$ **if** $n$ is divisible by $5$. **[1]**

&nbsp;&nbsp;(c) $n^2$ is even **if and only if** $n$ is even. **[1]**

*Answer form: true or false, plus a counterexample where false.*

::: {.workspace style="min-height:6cm"}

# Section B — Exam standard

## Question 4 **[4]**

Assume this statement is **true**:

> *If a shape is a square, then it has four equal sides.*

State what, if anything, you can conclude in each case. Write "nothing" where nothing follows.

&nbsp;&nbsp;(a) The shape is a square. **[1]**

&nbsp;&nbsp;(b) The shape has four equal sides. **[1]**

&nbsp;&nbsp;(c) The shape does **not** have four equal sides. **[1]**

&nbsp;&nbsp;(d) The shape is **not** a square. **[1]**

::: {.workspace style="min-height:6cm"}
Working
:::

## Question 5 **[4]**

For a real number $x$, consider the statement

> $x > 3$ **only if** $x^2 > 9$.

&nbsp;&nbsp;(a) Rewrite the statement in the form "if … then …". **[1]**

&nbsp;&nbsp;(b) Is the statement true? Justify your answer. **[1]**

&nbsp;&nbsp;(c) Write down the statement obtained by replacing "only if" with "if". Is *that* statement
true? If not, give a counterexample. **[2]**

## Question 6 **[6]**

In this question, $n$ is a positive integer. Consider the theorem

$$\text{If } n \text{ is divisible by } 12, \text{ then } n \text{ is divisible by } 4. \tag{$*$}$$

Which of the following, **taken individually**, is/are equivalent to $(*)$?

&nbsp;&nbsp;**I** &nbsp; If $n$ is divisible by $4$, then $n$ is divisible by $12$.

&nbsp;&nbsp;**II** &nbsp; $n$ is divisible by $12$ **only if** $n$ is divisible by $4$.

&nbsp;&nbsp;**III** &nbsp; $n$ is **not** divisible by $4$ **only if** $n$ is **not** divisible by $12$.

&nbsp;&nbsp;**A** I only &nbsp;&nbsp; **B** II only &nbsp;&nbsp; **C** III only &nbsp;&nbsp;
**D** I and II &nbsp;&nbsp; **E** II and III &nbsp;&nbsp; **F** I and III &nbsp;&nbsp;
**G** I, II and III &nbsp;&nbsp; **H** None of them

**Name the two halves $P$ and $Q$ before you start.** Show your arrows. **[6]**

::: {.workspace style="min-height:9cm"}
Working
:::

# Section C — Stretch

## Question 7 **[5]**

Here is an attempt to solve the inequality $x^4 - 10x^2 + 9 < 0$.

> $x^4 - 10x^2 + 9 < 0$
> **I** &nbsp; if and only if &nbsp; $(x^2-1)(x^2-9) < 0$
> **II** &nbsp; if and only if &nbsp; $1 < x^2 < 9$
> **III** &nbsp; if and only if &nbsp; $1 < x < 3$

&nbsp;&nbsp;(a) State which line contains the **first** error, or say that the argument is completely
correct. **[1]**

&nbsp;&nbsp;(b) Justify your answer, and give the correct solution set. **[4]**

::: {.workspace style="min-height:9cm"}
Working
:::

## Question 8 **[3]**

Let $A$ and $B$ be statements. A student writes:

> "Since $A \Rightarrow B$ is true, and $B$ is true, it follows that $A$ is true."

&nbsp;&nbsp;(a) Is the student's reasoning valid? **[1]**

&nbsp;&nbsp;(b) Give a concrete example, using statements about integers, that shows what goes wrong (or
explain why nothing goes wrong). **[2]**
